title: Binary search trees
objective: Search a tree by going left for smaller and right for bigger, following just one path.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): binary search trees

simplifies: This tree isn't kept balanced. Inserting keys in sorted order makes a long chain, and searches become slow. Balanced trees (AVL, red-black) fix that.

quiz.prompt: Searching a balanced search tree of 1,000,000 keys takes about…

options.explanation: Right. Each step goes down one level, and a balanced tree of a million keys is about 20 levels deep.
That is checking every key. The ordering means only one path is followed.
Only the root is one step away; most keys are deeper.

quiz.prompt: You insert 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in that order. What shape is the tree?

options.explanation: Right. Each key is bigger than the last, so every key goes right, and searches become linear.
Nothing rebalances it here; sorted input makes it lopsided.
Bigger keys go right, not left.
